correctness.rationale: Three-object one-extension geometric patterns are exhausted by the P/P/P, P/P/L, P/L/L, L/L/L split, with explicit exceptions q(q-2)=0 only in the Fano plane, and two-prefix extension completeness in dimension >=3 follows from 3-space incidence constructions and positive q(q-1)^2(q+1) skew line count. Backwards Hintikka recursion gives uniform rank-four equivalence. Rank-three skew line and rank-four concurrent uncovered-point sentences distinguish classes. 14/26/50 representative sizes follow from Gaussian counts. Exact finite recursion checked on six prime-field examples.

originality.rationale: The exact rank-four three-class classification across all finite projective planes and higher-dimensional finite projective spaces was not implied by the accessible prior claims or the inspected first-order/modal/geometric sources. An existing observation of Fano-versus-ternary plane separation is acknowledged as covered, not claimed as novel. Search incompleteness and partially inaccessible plausible texts are disclosed.
residual_risks: Stebletsova (1998), Modal logic of projective geometries of finite dimension, Technical Report 184, was cited by Venema but the report full text was not retrieved; language is described as collinearity modal, likely inapplicable, but definitive noncoverage is not claimed.
